newsitem.title: GERMANY: IG Metall says reached regional deal on sick pay.
newsitem.headline: IG Metall says reached regional deal on sick pay.

text.p: German engineering union IG Metall said on Thursday it had reached a deal with metal employers in a dispute about planned cuts in sick pay.

Talks covering 90,000 metal workers in the state of Lower Saxony had resumed at short notice on Wednesday with both sides saying they hoped a solution could be found at a regional level after national talks collapsed in October.
IG Metall and employer representatives said they had agreed to maintain sick pay at 100 percent, to pay a wage increase and had also agreed on rules for overtime and holiday bonuses.

IG Metall's regional leader Juergen Peters told a news conference after 13 hours of talks that under the deal, overtime and overtime bonuses would no longer be taken into account when calculating sick pay in future.
Wages for metalworkers in Lower Saxony will be increased by 1.5 percent from April 1, 1997 and by a further 2.5 percent from April 1, 1998.
Several other regional attempts at reaching a deal have failed recently.
IG Metall has been at the forefront of opposition to the sick pay cut to 80 percent which was made possible by legislation which came into force in October.
The union has staged walkouts involving hundreds of thousands of workers and has threatened to strike.
